security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU implements the mcsps CSR with a WARL write mask that forces SP[3:2] to zero (enforcing the old 128b/16B alignment), but guest software relies on the new spec where only SP[1:0] must be zero (4B alignment). When the guest writes a 4B-aligned SP value with non-zero bits [3:2] (e.g., SP=0x80000008), QEMU silently clears bits [3:2] to produce SP=0x80000000, corrupting the stack pointer used for conditional stack swaps.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: mcsps WARL write mask AND SP[3:2] forced-to-zero AND ~(ext_smcsps alignment assumed 128b)
security_spec.summary: mcsps SP field width changed from SP[XLEN-1:4] to SP[XLEN-1:2]; QEMU's WARL write mask must only zero bits [1:0] (4B alignment) not bits [3:0] (128b alignment), else guest SP values with non-zero bits [3:2] are silently corrupted

findings.finding: The Smcsps extension (mcsps CSR) is not implemented in this QEMU tree. Only CSR_SSP (for Zicfiss supervisor-mode shadow stack) is registered at line 5905. No CSR_MSP, read_msp, or write_msp exists. The described vulnerability (WARL write mask forcing SP[3:2] to zero on mcsps writes) is N/A because the target CSR does not exist to audit.
findings.snippet:
/* zicfiss Extension, shadow stack register */
    [CSR_SSP]  = { "ssp", cfi_ss, read_ssp, write_ssp },

findings.finding: Only CSR_SSP (0x011) is defined for Zicfiss. There is no CSR_MSP definition. The Smcsps extension and its mcsps CSR address are not defined in this header. No WARL alignment mask vulnerability applies.
